[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Capability count grows quickly in distributed development ecosystems. Without portfolio rationalization, portfolio sprawl produces capability overlap, high support burden, low reuse, and an ungovernable portfolio.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

Institutionalize split, merge, contain, and retire decisions using five objective criteria: overlap threshold, usage threshold, quality threshold, ownership threshold, and validation recency threshold. Apply these decisions through the portfolio registry and governance review cadence.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- When a capability meets one or more rationalization trigger conditions per STD-GOV-AI-005
- During monthly domain hygiene reviews, quarterly enterprise consolidation reviews, and annual domain topology reassessments
- When a new capability proposal would create a duplicate or near-duplicate of an existing registered capability
page_texts.7:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- Portfolio size is bounded by objective criteria rather than accumulating by default
- Duplicate intent coverage is visible and addressable before it creates inconsistent user experience
- Contained and retired lifecycle states are actively used rather than avoided
page_texts.9:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

Distributed teams in a citizen developer ecosystem can propose and build capabilities faster than governance capacity can review them. The natural result is capability accumulation: capabilities are added but rarely removed, overlapping capabilities are built independently, and ownerless capabilities remain in Production without a maintenance commitment.
page_texts.10:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

The M365 Copilot platform presents agents to users based on their discoverability configuration. A portfolio with many overlapping agents creates user confusion about which agent to use and produces inconsistent outputs for semantically equivalent requests. The governance registry must actively identify and resolve overlap to maintain the portfolio's usability and governance integrity.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

Without portfolio rationalization:
- New capabilities are proposed and built without checking whether existing capabilities already address the same intents
- Capabilities remain in Production long after their usage has dropped below any meaningful threshold
- No owner can be reached to make decisions about aging capabilities
- The portfolio becomes difficult to audit, support, or improve because its boundaries are undefined
page_texts.12:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- Teams resist retiring capabilities they built — even when usage data justifies retirement
- Rationalization decisions require objective criteria to be accepted as governance rather than arbitrary control
- Retirement requires successor mapping, which takes time and coordination
page_texts.14:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

Use five objective thresholds to drive rationalization decisions. When any threshold condition is met, the capability enters active rationalization review. The governance team and domain owner produce a disposition — one of: merge, split, contain, or retire — with a documented rationale and plan.

**Rationalization thresholds (from STD-GOV-AI-005):**

1. High overlap with an existing registered capability confirmed by overlap analysis
2. Usage volume below the defined minimum threshold for the relevant reporting period
3. Defect rate or rework rate exceeding the capability's quality rubric thresholds for two consecutive review cycles
4. No active owner assigned
5. Validation date stale beyond the review cadence defined in the domain governance documentation

**Disposition options:**

| Disposition | When to Use | Requirements |
|---|---|---|
| Merge | High overlap; two capabilities serve semantically equivalent intents | Migration plan, user communication plan, successor assignment |
| Split | A capability has grown beyond a single coherent business outcome | Two or more new capability contracts, migration plan |
| Contain | Usage below threshold; awaiting decision; ownership gap | Contained lifecycle state; owner assignment required to restore |
| Retire | Capability is no longer needed; successor exists or gap is accepted | Successor mapping or explicit gap acceptance; archive record |

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#architecture-diagram]

### Architecture Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Monthly Domain\nHygiene Review] --> B[Evaluate Capabilities\nvs 5 Trigger Conditions]
    B --> C{Trigger\nCondition Met?}
    C -- No --> D[Update Registry\nNo Action]
    C -- Yes --> E[Open Rationalization\nReview]
    E --> F{Disposition}
    F -- Merge --> G[Migration Plan +\nUser Communication]
    F -- Split --> H[Two New Capability\nContracts + Migration]
    F -- Contain --> I[Contained State\nOwner Required\nto Restore]
    F -- Retire --> J[Successor Mapping\nor Gap Acceptance\nArchive Record]
    G & H & I & J --> K[Execute via Change\nGateway STD-GOV-AI-004]
```
page_texts.16:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| Portfolio registry | Tracks rationalization trigger conditions for all capabilities | STD-GOV-AI-005 |
| Rationalization trigger monitoring | Evaluates registry data against threshold conditions | STD-GOV-AI-005, STD-TEC-AI-006 |
| Portfolio review cadence | Monthly/quarterly/annual review governance | STD-GOV-AI-005 |
| Disposition plan | Documents merge/split/contain/retire decision and execution plan | STD-GOV-AI-004 (change record for lifecycle state transitions) |
page_texts.17:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

1. Monthly domain hygiene review evaluates all active capabilities against the five rationalization trigger conditions
2. Capabilities meeting one or more trigger conditions are flagged for active rationalization review
3. Domain owner and governance reviewer produce a disposition — merge, split, contain, or retire — with a documented rationale
4. Disposition execution is governed by the change control process per STD-GOV-AI-004: Contain and Retire dispositions follow the ownership/lifecycle-change approval tier (domain owner approval); only a Split or Merge that results in a lifecycle state promotion for a resulting capability requires quality gate sign-off
5. Retired capabilities are archived in the registry with a successor mapping or explicit gap acceptance record
page_texts.18:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

- **New proposal overlap check**: run the rationalization overlap analysis proactively at proposal time, before investment in build, to detect new-proposal overlaps
- **Cross-domain rationalization**: the quarterly enterprise consolidation review identifies overlap across domain boundaries that the monthly domain review misses
page_texts.20:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#prerequisites]

### Prerequisites

- Portfolio registry active with all required fields current for all capabilities
- Rationalization trigger thresholds defined in domain governance documentation (usage minimums, validation staleness definition)
- Merge and retirement process templates available
page_texts.22:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#phase-1-baseline-portfolio-assessment]

#### Phase 1: Baseline Portfolio Assessment

1. Evaluate all existing capabilities against the five rationalization trigger conditions
2. Produce an initial rationalization status for each capability that meets a trigger condition
3. Assign each triggered capability a disposition and timeline
page_texts.23:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#phase-2-ongoing-rationalization-governance]

#### Phase 2: Ongoing Rationalization Governance

1. Monthly: review all registry records for new trigger condition occurrences; open rationalization reviews for newly triggered capabilities
2. Quarterly: evaluate cross-domain overlap; assess capabilities that have been in rationalization review for multiple months without resolution
3. Annually: reassess the domain topology — are the domain boundaries still aligned with the enterprise AI taxonomy?
page_texts.24:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#phase-3-disposition-execution]

#### Phase 3: Disposition Execution

1. Merge: produce a migration plan and user communication plan; update registry records; submit lifecycle state change as a governance gateway entry per STD-GOV-AI-004
2. Retire: produce a successor mapping or explicit gap acceptance; update registry with retirement date; archive the record
3. Contain: move to Contained lifecycle state; communicate to users; require owner assignment before restoration to Production
page_texts.25:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- Present rationalization decisions as objective findings backed by registry data, not as governance judgments about a team's work
- Define the disposition timelines in advance — an open rationalization review with no timeline produces no outcome
- Track the retirement-to-creation ratio as a leading indicator of portfolio health; a portfolio that never retires is accumulating debt
page_texts.26:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- Treating rationalization as a one-time cleanup exercise rather than an ongoing governance cadence
- Allowing rationalization reviews to remain open indefinitely without a disposition decision — indefinitely-open reviews are effectively deferrals
- Allowing teams to appeal rationalization decisions without objective counter-evidence — dispositions made without objective criteria are vulnerable to successful appeals that reintroduce the problem

page_texts.29:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#compliance-requirements]

### Compliance Requirements

- Monthly domain hygiene review is mandatory per STD-GOV-AI-005
- Rationalization trigger conditions must be evaluated against current registry data at each review
- Retirement requires successor mapping or explicit gap acceptance — silent retirement is not permitted
page_texts.30:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#approval-process]

### Approval Process

- Disposition decisions are reviewed by domain owner and governance team jointly
- Lifecycle state transitions (including Contain and Retire) follow the ownership or lifecycle state change tier in the approval matrix per STD-GOV-AI-004
page_texts.31:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#monitoring-and-metrics]

### Monitoring and Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
|---|---|---|
| Retirement-to-creation ratio | Increasing over time as portfolio matures | Portfolio registry counts |
| Capability reuse rate | Increasing over time | Usage metrics per STD-TEC-AI-006 |
| Duplicate capabilities in Production | Declining over time | Monthly overlap analysis |
| Open rationalization reviews without disposition | Zero beyond defined timeline | Monthly hygiene review |
page_texts.34:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#scenario-1-low-usage-capability-retirement]

#### Scenario 1: Low-usage capability retirement

During the monthly domain hygiene review, a capability is flagged for low usage over two consecutive monthly periods. No active owner can be reached. The governance reviewer opens a rationalization review. The domain lead confirms the capability is no longer actively used, identifies no active users requiring migration, and records an explicit gap acceptance. The capability is moved to Retired state and archived.
page_texts.35:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#scenario-2-overlap-merge]

#### Scenario 2: Overlap merge

The quarterly enterprise consolidation review identifies two capabilities in different domains that address semantically equivalent intents. The governance team presents the overlap analysis to both domain owners. The owners agree that one capability will be the surviving capability. A migration plan and user communication plan are produced. The retiring capability is Contained while the migration is executed, then Retired with the surviving capability as the successor.
page_texts.37:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#before-problem-state]

#### Before (Problem State)

The portfolio accumulates capabilities over time with no retirement process. Duplicate capabilities proliferate. Users do not know which agent to use. Support burden is distributed across many low-usage capabilities.
page_texts.38:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#after-solution-state]

#### After (Solution State)

The portfolio is actively governed through objective rationalization criteria and a regular review cadence. Dispositions are documented. The portfolio size is bounded. Duplicate capability rate trends downward over time.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-009-portfolio-rationalization-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Federated capability portfolios accumulate overlap, ownerless capabilities, and low-usage artifacts without a systematic way to remove them.

**Solution:** Use objective thresholds (overlap, usage, quality, ownership, validation recency) to identify rationalization candidates at each governance review; produce a disposition (merge/split/contain/retire) with a documented plan.

**When to Use:** Monthly domain hygiene reviews, quarterly enterprise consolidation reviews, new capability proposals with confirmed overlap.

**Key Benefits:**
- Portfolio sprawl is bounded by objective criteria
- Duplicate capability rate trends downward
- Contained and Retired lifecycle states are actively used

**Implementation Complexity:** Medium

**Prerequisites:** Portfolio registry active with current data, rationalization thresholds defined, review cadence established

**Related Patterns:** PTN-TEC-AI-008 Capability Cell, PTN-GOV-AI-012 Federated Change Gateway, PTN-GOV-AI-011 Telemetry-to-Governance Feedback
